lines: Avery Brooks
+1 (555) 010-3319 | avery.brooks@example.com | example.com/in/abrooks
Date of birth: 9 Jan 1998 | Nationality: Brazilian
EDUCATION
Eastmoor University | B.S. in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Riverside Cinema | Box Office Attendant | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Sold tickets and concessions during evening shifts and balanced the cash drawer at close.
- Trained 3 new attendants on the ticketing system and the refund policy.
Brightcart Retail | Data Analyst | Metro City, USA | Aug 2022 - Jun 2025
- Built the weekly retention dashboard for 2.4M customers that marketing used to retarget lapsed buyers, lifting 90-day repeat purchase from 22% to 27%.
- Cut the monthly revenue report from 3 days of spreadsheet work to 2 hours by moving it to scheduled SQL queries and a shared dashboard.
- Found customers with no orders by left-joining the orders table to the customers table and counting rows with a null customer name.

- Joining 40 source tables, deduplicating customer records across two loyalty systems and rebuilding the attribution logic in dbt-style SQL models, raised the share of orders tied to a campaign from 58% to 81%.
- Presented the quarterly customer review to the leadership team, and two of its three recommendations were funded in the next budget.
- Trained 20 merchandisers to answer their own questions with the self-serve dashboards, halving ad hoc data requests.
Pinecrest Insurance | Junior Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Jul 2022
- Ran the checkout A/B test until significance by checking the p-value every day and stopping on the first day it fell below 0.05.
- Analyzed 18 months of call-center data; my findings moved two agents to the evening peak and cut average hold time from 9 to 5 minutes.
- Writes the team's SQL style guide and review checklist, which cut query errors found in review by half.

- Automated the monthly fraud-flag extract while also maintaining the team calendar, answering ad hoc questions from sales, updating onboarding documents and covering the help desk on Fridays, which saved the fraud team 10 hours a month.
PROJECTS
City Bike-Share Demand Study | Independent Project | Python, SQL | Jan 2025 - Present
- Modeled hourly bike-share demand for 120 stations from 2 years of public trip data, forecasting next-day demand within 12% mean absolute error.
- Cut empty-station hours from 300 to 200 a week, a 50% reduction, in a replay of last summer's rebalancing.
- Raised forecast hit rate by 15% across 120 stations, from 60% to 75%, by adding weather and event features.
Food Pantry Visit Analysis | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Excel, SQL | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Mapped 14 months of pantry visits by hour and day, so the pantry moved one volunteer shift and cut the Saturday line from 50 to 20 minutes.
- Cleaned 9,000 handwritten visit logs into a single table and matched repeat visitors, giving the pantry its first count of unique households.
- Wrote a one-page guide the pantry coordinator used to update the visit table each month after the project ended.
SKILLS
Tools: SQL, Python, Excel
Methods: dashboards, forecasting, metric design, data-quality checks

items.says: The résumé includes date of birth and nationality, personal details conventionally omitted.
items.because: They are not evidence of analytical ability, invite unrelated judgments, and use valuable space.

items.says: The section order makes the degree and unrelated current job more prominent than the analytics experience.
items.because: It makes the candidate appear less experienced and gives the wrong first impression about their direction.

items.says: The routine box-office duties lack an outcome, operational scale, or specific system.
items.because: A reader cannot judge the volume or accuracy of the work, so the duties contribute little to the analytics story.

items.says: The training bullet gives the number trained but not the result of the training.
items.because: It does not show whether the attendants became independent or met a readiness standard.

items.says: The training bullet should lead the Riverside entry.
items.because: It is the clearer transferable responsibility.

items.says: The retention-dashboard bullet needs a compact technical or analytical detail.
items.because: “Built” does not reveal the method behind the result.

items.says: The join is backwards for finding customers with no orders.
items.because: Left-joining orders to customers cannot retain customers who have no orders.

items.says: A null customer name is the wrong field to identify customers with no orders.
items.because: It would generally indicate an order that failed to match a customer.

items.says: The customer-without-orders finding lacks its scale and business consequence.
items.because: The reader cannot judge what changed because of the finding, so it reads like a technical exercise.

items.says: The attribution bullet makes the methods the grammatical subject and buries the 58%-to-81% result.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the impact and the candidate’s ownership.

items.says: The leadership-review bullet does not show the analysis behind the funded recommendations.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether the candidate performed the analysis that produced them.

items.says: The A/B test uses an invalid significance procedure.
items.because: Daily checks of an unadjusted p-value with stopping below 0.05 create multiple opportunities for a false positive.

items.says: The A/B-test line does not state the test’s business result.
items.because: Statistical significance does not show whether checkout conversion, revenue, or another product outcome improved.

items.says: The call-center bullet puts the method before the stronger result.
items.because: The staffing change and hold-time reduction are more likely to catch a recruiter’s attention.

items.says: “My findings” uses a first-person pronoun.
items.because: It breaks the résumé’s otherwise impersonal phrasing.

items.says: “Writes” is the wrong tense for a role that ended in July 2022.
items.because: Present tense conflicts with the dated position and makes the timeline inconsistent.

items.says: The long list of secondary duties obscures the fraud-extract automation achievement.
items.because: The main achievement loses prominence among unrelated responsibilities.

items.says: The source of the 10-hour monthly saving is unclear.
items.because: A reader may not know whether it came from the fraud extract or the combined duties.

items.says: “Ad hoc questions” is vague filler.
items.because: It does not identify the type of sales support.

items.says: The demand-modeling bullet does not show the modeling approach.
items.because: The reader cannot see the technical work behind the accuracy result.

items.says: The demand-modeling bullet does not say what the forecast enabled.
items.because: Without a connection to a decision, the result remains a project metric rather than evidence of practical use.

items.says: The claimed 50% reduction from 300 to 200 hours is arithmetically wrong.
items.because: A reduction of 100 out of 300 hours is 33.3%.

items.says: “Cut” presents a replay as if it were a real operational reduction.
items.because: The result came from a replay of last summer’s rebalancing.

items.says: The replay method is not explained.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what policy or rule produced the simulated result.

items.says: The change from 60% to 75% is 15 percentage points, not 15%.
items.because: The relative increase is 25%.

items.says: “Hit rate” is undefined.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what counted as a correct forecast.

items.says: The pantry-shift sentence makes the causal connection and shift change awkward.
The unique-household result does not state how many households were identified.
The guide’s continued use is not quantified.
